text: Here is the result of "fetch" for the Page with URL https://app.notion.com/p/41b4a78a1c8781e88b9eedaaf8354377 as of 2026-11-19T22:49:43.631Z: {"Category":"ops","Last edited":"2026-11-19T22:49:43.631Z","Name":"Inference footguns","Priority":"p1","Status":"In progress","date:Period:is_datetime":0,"date:Period:start":"2026-11-17","url":"https://app.notion.com/p/41b4a78a1c8781e88b9eedaaf8354377"} {"type":"emoji","emoji":"🦶"} # Plan Static sweep of reductoai/api @ 4df0566ccd (code and config only, no telemetry or PostHog values read). 8 findings, ranked by impact x confidence. - Fixing now - (1) Autoscaler queue signal: the KEDA trigger is dynamo_frontend_active_requests per worker against activeRequestsTarget, so it tops out at seats / target (1.25x for R-1 35B, 1.375x for Maverick) however deep the router queue is - Fix: add the router's admit queue to the trigger (in-flight plus queued per worker) - ✅ (2) Router share defaults, done in [#15184](https://github.com/reductoai/api/pull/15184): Triton, Magpie, citation 7B and FigSum are share_pct: 0 in router.prod.yaml, the live share exists only in PostHog, so a missing value or a pod that cannot read the flag store sends them 100% to Modal with no log - Fix: commit each ramped share as the YAML default (as Maverick and R-1 already do at 100), PostHog stays the override - (3) dfine_table_model batching benchmark: the cluster build is forced to batch 1, delay 0, while checkbox runs batch 10 on cluster and batch 1 on Modal - Fix: benchmark batch > 1 on H200, or record why batch 1 is required - ✅ (5) FallbackBackend, done in [#15185](https://github.com/reductoai/api/pull/15185): falls through on any exception, so a deterministic input error on Modal runs again on the CPU LOCAL\_SERVICE; only a logfire.warn, no counter - Fix: no fall-through on non-retryable error types, count fallbacks by method and backend - ✅ (8) together-inference delete, done in [#15182](https://github.com/reductoai/api/pull/15182): together-inference/ looks dead (static replicas: 13, deploy/models last changed 2026-02, no prod code references it) - Fix: confirm it is retired, delete the directory - Not fixing now - (11) Watch, no fix proposed: a Dynamo frontend answers 404 during a worker rollout while its /capacity still reports seats. Maverick on gcp_usw3, 2026-11-19 07:31 PT: 300 of 1,896 calls in one minute got 404 as the cap went 192 to 48 to 144; each went to Modal. 12 more on gcp_uss1 the hour of 22:00 PT Nov 18. A 404 is not a fault for the down flag - (4) Down flag needs 20 results and 50% errors per router pod: a cluster failing under half its calls never trips, low-traffic namespaces never reach 20 results per pod (known tradeoff) - (6) Triton call budgets stack: 45 s cluster, then a fresh 45 s for Modal, then LOCAL\_SERVICE, instead of one shared deadline (documented) - (7) AU drift: AU serves 2B int8_20261019 against nvfp4_20261023 in US and EU, and 3 to 6 AU router pods serve nothing (no AU route) ## Modal ingress limit: split any Modal server (R-1 mini first) (finding 10) Ask: Jean's stamp. Nothing is built. The plan is on its own page: Modal ingress limit: split any Modal server (R-1 mini first) # Logs - \[\] Sweep done, 8 findings. Fixes picked: 1, 2, 3, 5, 8. No PRs yet. - \[\] Finding 8: [#15182](https://github.com/reductoai/api/pull/15182) ✅ merged by Jean. Deletes the retired together-inference/ directory. - \[\] Finding 5: [#15185](https://github.com/reductoai/api/pull/15185) ✅ merged by Jean. FallbackBackend fails at once on InputError and ProcessingError instead of trying the next backend, and counts fallbacks in reducto.inference.backend_fallbacks by method, backend and error type. - \[\] Finding 9 added from the Basis burst of 14:52 to 14:54 PT (Tinybird traces and controller gauges): the admit-deadline spill put about 1,340 requests on 3 Modal R1 containers in 20 s, median 135 s in vLLM's queue, 942 cancelled at 97 s. Scale-up fired (15 containers by 14:55:07 PT) but after the wave and at the drain_s size. Fix (a) or (b) is Jean's pick. - \[\] Finding 9 fix (c): [#15195](https://github.com/reductoai/api/pull/15195) open. The R1 wrapper cancels a buffered completion when its caller disconnects; before, FastAPI kept the handler running and vLLM generated the page for nobody. - \[\] Found while measuring for #15185: [#15188](https://github.com/reductoai/api/pull/15188) ✅ merged by Jean. The consolidated Triton client caps every wire request at 256 images, so a predict over the limit splits instead of failing with InvalidConfigError (279 images go out as 256 + 23). Not deployed yet. - \[\] Finding 2: [#15184](https://github.com/reductoai/api/pull/15184) ✅ merged by Jean. The YAML share_pct of every namespace with its own PostHog share value is now the live value, 100 for all 12 (US: the 4 Triton pools, Magpie, citation 7B, FigSum; EU: FigSum, Magpie, citation 7B, R-1, R-1 mini, maverick), and a missing value warns inference_router.missing_share once a minute per flag per process. No deploy by the session: it takes effect with the next prod release. - \[\] Finding 9 fix (c): [#15195](https://github.com/reductoai/api/pull/15195) ✅ approved by Jean and merged. Not live until the next fpp-flash deploy; then check on stg that a cancelled call logs fpp.request.abandoned and leaves no llm_request span past the cancel. Fix (a) or (b) is still Jean's pick. - \[\] Finding 9: Jean keeps the spill as it is (no cap, no Modal pre-sizing), so (a) and (b) are dropped. Cluster path checked for the same bug, no fix needed: the router stops the provider call when the worker hangs up (TestAWorkerThatHangsUpStopsTheProviderCall), and the Dynamo 1.5.1 worker in the running prod image aborts the vLLM request when its context is stopped (dynamo/vllm/handlers.py _monitor_abort). On prod-gpu-use1 since its pods started 4 days ago: 9 dynamo_frontend_disconnected_clients, 9 frontend requests with error_type=cancelled, 9 worker dynamo_component_cancellation_total on generate, in 4.09M requests. Not observed: a GPU seat freed by a dropped call (no stg or dev GPU cluster; would need one test page on a prod cluster). The stg check of the Modal fix still waits on the next fpp-flash deploy. - \[\] Finding 9 fix (c) checked on stg (fpp-flash v181, has [#15195](https://github.com/reductoai/api/pull/15195)): ✅ pass. 5 long pages dropped 3 s in: 5 fpp.request.abandoned, no llm_request span for any of them. 24 dropped at once (20 running, 4 queued in vLLM): 24 abandoned, running and waiting counts at 0 within 1.2 s of the drop, no llm_request span. Control page with the caller connected: 200, 15,561 tokens in 7.7 s. Before the fix (v180) the same 5 dropped pages each ran 10 to 11 s to the end. vLLM's abort counter stayed 0 and I read no abort log line. Prod fpp-flash v135 (16:25 PT) has the fix; no Modal R-1 call has been dropped there since, so nothing to confirm in prod yet. - \[\] R-1 35B A100 80GB profile (a100-fp8-tp1): [#15230](https://github.com/reductoai/api/pull/15230) open. Adds the 1, 8 and 16 in-flight rows, measured on one A100 80GB on Modal dev with the arm 05 recipe (memory 0.92): 0.39, 1.00 and 1.13 pages/s, p50 2.0, 6.1 and 10.1 s, 1.772, 0.696 and 0.612 USD per 1k pages, 0 errors. Adds the recipe vllm-35b-fp8-a100 and a dev-only Modal host; no pick names it, so nothing deploys. Not tested: a full R1 boot through fpp-flash on an A100. - \[\] R-1 35B single-H100 profile (h100-fp8-tp1, FP8 weights, no TP2): [#15237](https://github.com/reductoai/api/pull/15237) open. Adds the recipe vllm-35b-h100-fp8 and a Modal host (H100!, dev and prod\_au); no pick names it, AU untouched. Re-measured on one H100 on Modal dev with the tuned MoE config: 0.69, 2.32, 3.07, 3.13, 3.19, 3.14 and 3.15 pages/s at 1, 8, 16, 32, 48, 64 and 96 in flight, p50 1.1, 2.6, 3.9, 8.7, 13.6, 18.7 and 28.8 s, 0 errors; 0.357 USD per 1k pages at 16 in flight against 0.131 for the B200 1112 package (13.26 pages/s). Judge against 1112 on rep-1k: 7 wins, 981 ties, 12 losses, net -5 (bar -30). A dev shadow built from the branch served a page on an H100 and restored from its GPU snapshot in 100 s; it is stopped. Not checked: H100 capacity in Modal AU. - \[\] R-1 35B single-H100 profile, re-measured with the shared AIPerf runner (rep-1k, 180 s per level, dev shadow of the R1 class held at one container, load through the Modal proxy): 0.68, 2.11, 2.84, 3.05, 3.00, 3.00 and 3.09 pages/s at 1, 8, 16, 32, 48, 64 and 96 in flight; p90 2.5, 5.7, 8.6, 14.0, 18.5, 23.9 and 33.8 s; 0 errors. The gate (p90 at most 10 s, no error) passes up to 16 in flight: 0.387 USD per 1k pages, 3.0 times the B200 1112 package. The table in [#15237](https://github.com/reductoai/api/pull/15237) now comes from this run. The runner gained --header-env so it can reach an fpp-flash shadow. The dev app is stopped. - \[\] R-1 35B single-H200 profile, [#15249](https://github.com/reductoai/api/pull/15249) open (variant h200-fp8-tp1, a measurement record: no recipe or host). The H100 FP8 TP1 package unchanged on one H200, shared AIPerf runner inside the container on [localhost](http://localhost), rep-1k, 1,000 requests per level, one run per level: 0.79, 2.66, 3.45, 3.70, 3.86, 3.95, 4.07, 4.35, 4.28 and 4.37 pages/s at 1, 8, 16, 20, 24, 28, 32, 48, 64 and 96 in flight; p90 2.1, 4.9, 7.8, 8.8, 10.3, 11.8, 12.9, 18.1, 21.8 and 29.1 s; 0 errors. The gate (p90 at most 10 s, no error) passes up to 20 in flight: 0.341 USD per 1k pages at 4.54 USD per hour, 2.6 times the B200 1112 package. At 16 in flight it is 3.45 pages/s and 0.365 USD per 1k against the H100's 2.84 and 0.387 (different load path: the H100 rows went through the Modal proxy). Judge against B200 BF16: 14 wins, 978 ties, 8 losses, net +6. More KV memory, FP8 KV and BF16 weights were screened on the workstream's old load loop only and gave no gain; the gate breaks on latency before the KV cache fills. The first table in this PR came from that old loop (4.61 pages/s peak at 64 in flight, outside the gate) and was replaced. Both dev apps are stopped. ### 2026-11-17 16:55 PT, daily router cost read (first run, partial) - Scope: 10 router apps. Modal side measured for all; cluster GPU cost and the inference-health page COGS not read (Datadog keys on the VM and in Doppler dev_alex return 403; the page refuses the session sign-in with requester_not_allowed). Asked Xavier for access. - Modal spend per 1k ok calls or pages, before vs after the move (Modal bill final through 11-15): Maverick 0.44 to 0.35; R-1 2.75 to 1.17; R-1 mini 1.40 to 4.81 (volume fell about 9x, Modal spend only halved). - Citation 7B, FigSum, Magpie, change tracking, highlight detection: first router grants on 11-17, baseline recorded, no verdict yet. - Triton calls served by usw1 write no model.call span and the snapshot counts no usw1 cost, so the page's Triton families are Modal only and read too high after the move. - On 11-17 the router sent about half of core CV and two thirds of Qwen RF-DETR grants to Modal, not usw1. - Sources: Snowflake EXTERNAL_APPS.MODAL.MODAL_USAGE_DAILY plus the Modal billing API; Tinybird otel_model_call_mv (countMergeIf(call_count, outcome = 'ok')); Tinybird otel_metrics_sum router.grants by namespace and cluster; family mapping from cloudflare/inference-health-internal/snapshot/config.yaml. Scripts and exact queries: bot memory files/router-cost-daily/README.md. - No code change, no PR. ### 2026-11-17 17:20 PT, daily router cost read (first run, full) - Cluster GPU cost added from Datadog (Jean's personal access token, Doppler dev_jean, read only). Rate 5.50 USD per GPU-hour for B200 and usw1 H200. Modal bill is final through 11-15; 11-16 and 11-17 are Modal API estimates. - USD per 1k ok calls or pages, before to after the move, Modal + cluster: - Maverick 0.66 to 0.55 (after 11-06..11-17) - R-1 3.73 to 2.25 (after 11-09..11-17) - R-1 mini 2.21 to 4.62 (after 11-09..11-17): regression, volume fell from 1.6M to 0.5M pages a day while cost fell from 3.6k to 2.3k USD a day - Triton core vision, US 1.35 to 0.84 (after 11-14..11-17) - Qwen RF-DETR, US 1.03 to 0.61 (after 11-14..11-17) - One estimated day of router traffic (11-17), no verdict: Citation 7B 2.28 to 2.71, FigSum 1.09 to 1.30, Magpie 14.54 to 7.31, change tracking 1.03 to 1.50, highlight detection 2.95 to 1.19 - inference-health page gaps: Triton calls through the router or to usw1 write no model.call row and usw1 GPU cost is not counted, so its Triton families are wrong after the move; the family regexes miss the Dynamo workloads fpp-2b-tiered, fpp-2b-snapshot and fpp-35b-snapshot, so R-1 mini reads 4.05 where 4.62 is right. - Sources added: Datadog kubernetes_state.deployment.replicas_available (dynamo-serving workers; usw1 triton-* deployments) and reducto.triton_flash.client_http_attempts (ok, by environment, target host, model). Scripts and exact queries: bot memory files/router-cost-daily/README.md. - Not done: live PostHog shares not read; the page's own COGS not read (sign-in refused), recomputed with its loaders and config instead. No code change, no PR. ### 2026-11-17 17:30 PT, daily router cost read (first run, follow-up) - Correction: R-1 mini is not a router regression. Its pages fell 15x on 11-04, five days before the move; USD per 1k pages was 1.60 at the high volume, 18.50 at the low volume just before the move, 4.62 after it. Seats were already keyed by namespace (-dynamo-load-summary). Open, CI green, Codex clean. - Left open: _clusters has no row-level test (it reads Datadog and Tinybird). ### 2026-11-17 18:05 PT, Modal share alert fired for prod\_eu fpp-2b - [#15233](https://github.com/reductoai/api/pull/15233): the 50% monitor and its 65% triton-qwen-rfdetr copy leave out cluster:unknown, so no environment is named. ✅ Approved by Jean, merged, and applied at 18:08 PT in [run-v0pg86u0ijfj11c7c](https://reducto.scalr.io/v2/e/env-v0p5qlbd4pjdjqdgj/workspaces/ws-v0p6k6p0hu0qqurf6/runs/run-v0pg86u0ijfj11c7c) (3 changed). - The Scalr plan also updates inference_router_all_clusters_down (29297426), the unapplied change of [#15209](https://github.com/reductoai/api/pull/15209), not this PR. Its own run (run-v0pg85iuqtkoffh8m) was canceled at 18:07 PT when this merge queued the next one, which applied it. ### 2026-11-18 08:35 PT, daily router cost read - Data through 11-17 UTC (the Modal bill for 11-17 is an API estimate), plus 11-18 00:00 to 16:00 UTC for the Modal bill and calls. Table and graph refreshed on the [router migration page](https://app.notion.com/p/4164a78a1c87818ea15bdef76227228c). No code change, no PR. - USD per 1k ok calls or pages, all regions, before to after the move, Modal + cluster GPUs: - Cheaper: Maverick 0.66 to 0.55, R-1 3.73 to 2.23, Qwen RF-DETR 0.75 to 0.43, Triton core vision 1.67 to 1.13 - One day of router traffic (11-17), no verdict: Magpie 14.54 to 7.31, highlight detection 3.99 to 1.64, Citation 7B 2.28 to 2.71, FigSum 1.09 to 1.30, change tracking 1.41 to 2.14 - R-1 mini 2.21 to 4.79, volume-driven. On 11-17 it had 1.48M pages and cost 1.55 - R-1 cluster cost does not follow volume. The fpp-35b workers went from about 31 to about 58 B200s on 11-13 (745 to 1,400 GPU-hours a day) and stayed at 56 to 60 every hour from 11-14 to 11-17, about 7.7k USD a day. US pages cost 1.53 and 1.61 on 11-16 and 11-17 (5.3M and 5.4M pages) but 3.91 and 5.21 on 11-14 and 11-15 (2.0M and 1.5M pages). Maverick shows the same on a floor of 12 workers: 1.09 and 1.34 on the weekend against 0.34 to 0.44 on weekdays. Why the workers do not scale down was not read. - Triton core vision: the "cheaper" verdict rests on the weekend. US cost 0.51 and 0.73 on 11-14 and 11-15 (2.5M and 1.7M calls) but 1.51 and 1.44 on 11-16 and 11-17, against 1.37 before the move. The US Modal bill of TritonFlashServer is 0.8k to 1.6k USD a day after the move against about 1.16k before, while the router released 88% to 98% of core vision leases to usw1. Qwen RF-DETR holds on weekdays (US 0.54 and 0.74 against 1.04). - Citation 7B, FigSum and Magpie have no cluster workers: every router.release is Modal, in US and EU, so only the Modal floor can move their cost. 11-17 is inside the 11-09 to 11-13 weekday range for Citation 7B (2.71 against 2.34 to 2.96) and FigSum (1.30 against 1.01 to 1.30). Change tracking US 1.53 is inside its range too (1.15 to 1.69); its 303 USD a day is fixed, so cost follows calls. - R-1 mini on 11-18: 1.2M pages went to Modal fpp-flash between 00:00 and 02:00 UTC (router.release: Modal 494k and 710k an hour, the three clusters 120k to 166k an hour together). It matches the load-test floor of [#15191](https://github.com/reductoai/api/pull/15191) (from 00:35 UTC), which is planned spend. US fpp-flash Modal bill 00:00 to 16:00 UTC: 1,886 USD against 553 for the same hours of 11-17. - Modal bill, 11-18 against 11-17, 00:00 to 16:00 UTC, other apps: US Citation 7B 957 against 1,296, FigSum 469 against 516, Magpie 232 against 306, Maverick 584 against 478, triton-flash 2,013 against 1,975. EU Citation 7B 301 against 167 on fewer calls (28k against 62k); EU Maverick 1,116 against 899 on 15% more calls. - Not done: the inference-health page's own COGS (sign-in refused on 11-17, not retried; recomputed with its loaders and config), live PostHog shares. - \[\] Finding 9 fix (c) confirmed in prod, read-only, on the Nov 17 load test spill after [#15195](https://github.com/reductoai/api/pull/15195) went live (16:25 PT): ✅ 299 direct Modal fpp-35b calls were cancelled by the worker (222 at 16:47 to 16:53 PT, 77 at 17:14 to 17:16 PT). All 299 reached the R1 wrapper; 297 logged fpp.request.abandoned a median 0.04 s (max 0.74 s) after the drop, and no llm_request for any of them ended more than 0.2 s past the drop. The other 2 had finished generating 0.15 and 0.26 s before the caller left, so there was nothing to cancel. In the Basis burst before the fix, about 750 of 942 were generated in full. Also seen: 72 of 95 cancelled R-1 mini calls on router-leased Modal seats match an abandoned event; the other 23 are not matched by my join, not checked further. Spilled pages still wait in vLLM's queue (31 and 59 s on the two I read), as expected with the spill left as it is. ### 2026-11-19 08:40 PT, daily router cost read - Data through 11-18 UTC (the Modal bill for 11-18 is an API estimate), plus 11-19 00:00 to 16:00 UTC for the Modal bill and calls. Table and graph refreshed on the [router migration page](https://app.notion.com/p/4164a78a1c87818ea15bdef76227228c). No code change, no PR. - USD per 1k ok calls or pages, all regions, before to after the move, Modal + cluster GPUs: - Cheaper: Maverick 0.66 to 0.51, R-1 3.73 to 2.21, Triton core vision 1.67 to 1.23, Qwen RF-DETR 0.75 to 0.42, Magpie 14.54 to 7.10, highlight detection 3.99 to 2.25 - Costlier (two days of router traffic, 11-17 and 11-18): FigSum 1.09 to 1.50, Citation 7B 2.28 to 2.51, change tracking 1.41 to 3.59, Maverick EU 1.05 to 1.17 - R-1 mini 2.21 to 2.16, volume-driven, no verdict. On 11-18 the US had 7.43M pages at 0.42 (load-test tiers of [#15232](https://github.com/reductoai/api/pull/15232) and [#15235](https://github.com/reductoai/api/pull/15235); 82% of fpp-2b releases went to Modal, 1,843 USD) - FigSum is the one regression that holds at equal volume. US: 752k calls cost 1,108 USD on 11-18 against 739 for 748k on 11-12; 1.15M cost 1,114 on 11-17 against 879 for 1.13M on 11-11. EU: 291k cost 767 on 11-17 against 536 for 280k on 11-13. Its Modal app billed 220 GPU-hours a day against 151 and ran at 3.0% utilization against 7.6% (US 3.7% against 7.8%, EU 2.1% against 7.4%). Likely cause: since the move the controller keeps 4.3 to 4.4 containers ready in the US and 3.2 to 3.6 in the EU (controller.capacity.ready, daily average, 11-17 to 11-19), where the cron held 1 + 1 at peak and 1 + 0 off peak. The buffer of 1 from [#15336](https://github.com/reductoai/api/pull/15336) went live on 11-19 at 01:39 UTC and adds to it: 11-19 to 16:00 UTC cost 1.55 in the US (649 USD for 419k calls) and 1.90 in the EU. - Citation 7B: the US is not a regression going forward. 11-17 cost 2.64 (raise mode until the 19:38 UTC release, 17.7 containers ready on average); 11-18, the first full day in slots mode ([#15050](https://github.com/reductoai/api/pull/15050)), cost 1.85 and 11-19 to 16:00 UTC 1.76, against 2.11 before. The EU is costlier: 514 USD for 40k calls on 11-18 against about 200 a day before, with 3.9 containers ready against 1.6 on 11-17. Likely cause: the EU controller sizes the pool since the EU route ([#15134](https://github.com/reductoai/api/pull/15134)) took traffic (slots mode, floor 1 in config.prod_eu.yaml) and holds more containers than the cron did; the mechanism is not confirmed. 11-19 to 16:00 UTC: 330 USD for 52k calls (6.40). - Change tracking US 1.05 to 2.82 is mostly volume: 198k and 120k calls against 183k to 273k on weekdays before, and usw1 is a fixed 137 USD a day. Its Modal bill was 419 USD on 11-17 (highlight detection 296) against 173 to 215, and back to 204 on 11-18, the first full day in slots mode ([#15142](https://github.com/reductoai/api/pull/15142)). - Maverick EU: 1.17 on both days (1,497 and 1,843 USD) against 0.75 to 1.08 on weekdays before; no cluster GPUs in the EU. Modal utilization 2.5% against 4.8%, 213 paid GPU-hours a day against 181. 11-19 to 16:00 UTC: 1,483 USD for 1.46M calls (1.02). Cause not found. - EU Triton core vision and Qwen RF-DETR got their first real router traffic on 11-19 (301k and 243k releases by 16:00 UTC), so they stay "not on the router" in this read. - Not done: the inference-health page's own COGS (sign-in refused on 11-17, not retried; recomputed with its loaders and config), live PostHog shares, the cause of the Maverick EU rise. ### 2026-11-19 10:00 PT, daily footgun hunt (first run) - Scope: the router client (src/lib/inference_router/client.py), the router proxy (inference-router/internal/proxy), the controller config of US prod, then 24 hours of router metrics in Tinybird (router.upstream.status, controller.capacity.errors) to 10:00 PT. dynamo-stable: not swept yet. - Checked, nothing to fix: capacity read errors are tens a day for each cluster; lease_unknown 887 of 5.9M fpp-35b calls; cluster 529s 784 of 5.9M; Magpie 400s 266 (request faults). - Not looked at yet: EU FigSum 502s from Modal (244), Triton core vision 503 and 500 from Modal (312 and 152), the router's admission scripts and mailbox, the controller's target rules, dynamo-stable. - 10:45 PT, second pass, no new find: - Router admission: read admit.lua, admit_low.lua and grant.lua; no bug.
